We need to call it twice for presidents: year 1980, position 'president'; year 2016, position 'president'. And twice for vice presidents: year 1975, position 'vice president'; year 2011, position 'vice president'.

We should call the function for each query. The function returns data. We need to combine results. The function signature: get_president_and_vp({year: number, position: string}). So we need to call four times.

We should output the results. The user likely expects names. Let's recall: 1980 US President was Jimmy Carter (1977-1981). 2016 US President was Barack Obama (2009-2017). Vice Presidents: 1975 Vice President was Walter Mondale (1977-1981) but in 1975 the VP was Gerald Ford? Wait: Gerald Ford was VP from 1973 to 1974, then became President. In 1975, the Vice President was Nelson Rockefeller? Actually after Ford became President in 1974, the VP position was vacant until 1975 when Nelson Rockefeller was appointed? Let's check: After Ford became President, the VP position was vacant until 1975 when Nelson Rockefeller was appointed as VP on March 25, 1975. So in 1975, the Vice President was Nelson Rockefeller. In 2011, Vice President was Joe Biden (2009-2017). So answer: 1980 President: Jimmy Carter; 2016 President: Barack Obama; 1975 Vice President: Nelson Rockefeller; 2011 Vice President: Joe Biden.
